member.name: T:Meziantou.Framework.Globbing.Glob
member.summary:
Glob patterns specify sets of filenames with wildcard characters. Supported syntaxes:
Wildcard Description
* matches any number of characters including none, excluding directory separator
? matches a single character
[abc] matches one character in the brackets
[!abc] matches any character not in the brackets
[a-z] matches one character from the range given in the brackets. GlobOptions.IgnoreCase is only supported for ASCII letters.
[!a-z] matches one character that is not from the range given in the brackets. GlobOptions.IgnoreCase is only supported for ASCII letters.
{abc,123} comma-delimited set of literals, matches 'abc' or '123'
** matches zero or more directories
!pattern leading '!' negates the pattern
\x escapes the following character. For instance, '\*' matches the literal character '*' instead of being a wildcard.
If the pattern ends with a /, only directories are matched. Otherwise, only files are matched.
Matching backtracks, so the cost of a single call grows exponentially with the number of * wildcards in one path segment. Ordinary patterns and file names are unaffected, but a pattern coming from an untrusted source can be made expensive on purpose. Bound the length and the wildcard count of such patterns before parsing them.
